Zip Zap Circus

By: Diana Lucas | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

Summary:
In 1992 trapeze artist Brent Van Rensberg had a dream, a circus school to teach kids the joy of performing. He wanted his circus school to focus on underprivileged children, children who might not see a future or might not have a future or simply needed something to get them off the streets. Brent’s passion came form a very personal place his own past was troubled and Brent himself was given a chance at a better life in a circus.

He called his project Dare to Dream: But in 1992 when we met up with Brent in Langa teaching kids circus skills and he put little Sizwe on a bar on a tree in Langa and taught him simple trapeze stunts…we may have thought pretty picture, lovely dream but this is not going anywhere.

We couldn’t have been more wrong, the Zip Zap circus has gone from strength to strength.


Further information:
In 1994 they toured -a simple but charismatic circus school - to the National Arts Festival in Grahamstown. Three years later they did a show for Mandela’s 77th birthday and then 1998 their first international tour to Denmark.

Since then they have performed to date 35 tours in 19 countries their next circus tour to France will be this September. Last year alone 2 042 children were being put through 8 different programmes. 4 outreach, 3 youth and 1 professional, all the children attended free of charge.

The Zip Zap children have performed for presidents and world leaders. Kids, who began as six-year-olds swinging from a trapeze tied to a tree, are now professional performing artists working in Europe and North America. Young people who grew up on the streets are now skilled and valued artists and technicians in the entertainment and film industries. Best of all, these kids have become teachers themselves. They are ambassadors and role models for others, demonstrating dramatically to young people and the wider public the possibility of a new way of treating each other.

Ibonglewthu is their outreach programme in partnership with Doctors without Borders, where they are working with children in Khayelitshe

Their latest venture with the Cape Philharmonic Orchestra, at the Artscape Opera House is the pivotal point of our story….how far they have come. We film their incredible feats in ‘Journey Beyond’. This is a major operatic performance intertwined with circus performance.

For years the goal was to get a permanent home for the circus school, today through the determination of Brent and his French wife Laurence they have a wonderful permanent home in Salt River..

We will profile some of the stars of the show like Phelelani Ndakokra, who grew up on the street and today is possibly the most talented performer at Zip Zap. His background is very sad, but he himself has become a role model at Zip Zap.
Other stars of the show who we will interview: Jacobus Claason ( Trompie) also joined Zip Zap from living on the street, he has been with Zip Zap fro 9 years and together with Jason Barnard performed at the White House in Washington DC for Barack Obama. They have also performed for Andy Murray and Roger Federer at a charity tennis match in Zurich last year.

We film their out Outreach programme, Ibonglewethu, that started in 2005…what they have achieved how are they making a difference. We can’t film the younger children because of the Child Protection Act but we can the older children and we will also talk to the SA Head of Doctors without Borders…it goes far beyond teaching circus skills to youngsters.

How do they do all this and still charge children nothing – the generosity of sponsors individuals, organizations, corporations, and foundations and they have the Dome, a show venue in town which generates a large portion of Zip Zap’s income to keep the school free of charge

Brent and Laurence are doers and have never stopped making their vision a reality over 25 years ago when we met them.

Since we met them they have had two daughters,. Sabine, their eldest is performing trapeze artist, she is with one of the top touring circus companies in the world called 7 Fingers. Saskia also a trapeze artist, she will be performing her final shows in the Philharmonic Opera Spectacular. But Saskia is leaving the circus world to study politics and law in a University in France.

Zip Zap is dedicated to supporting and conducting training in circus arts and performance as a powerful tool for social transformation, youth empowerment, team building and community upliftment. The programs provide opportunities for young South Africans from very different backgrounds to play, learn and live together using the medium of circus training and performance to model and demonstrate the possibility of true coexistence
it’s incredible to think that through their passion so many people have benefited they remain not wealthy in monetary terms but hundred times over with the love of this family they call Zip Zap

Script:


V/O 9 sec
Zip Zap Circus – joined forces last month with the Cape Town Philharmonic Orchestra and took audiences on a mesmerising journey.

V/O 4 sec
Zip Zap is a social circus academy, a non profit organisation.

Jacobus Claassen (Trompie),
Trompie: It feels like the whole world is hugging you with lots of love ..I love it.

V/O 6 sec
Trompie aka Jacobus Claassen is one of Zip Zap’s star performers.

Claire: What is the thing you are known for?
Trompie: Now I do a bit of everything but mainly I love to clown around.
Claire: Is it part of your personality?
Yaa my daily life.

V/O 10 sec
Trompie’s life looked very different 10 years ago, he was living in a shelter, it was an out reach programme that gave him an entirely new vision for his future.

Trompie: I have changed a lot because I was a very closed person not able to talk to anyone now I can talk to anyone since I came to ZZ I have been the most, friendliest guy ever.

Link: We were first introduced to ZZ 25 years ago when Brent and Laurence van Rensberg decided to open the social circus school it all started with a swing in a tree and a very big dream.

V/O
Brent Van Rensburg joined the circus when he was 11 years old, his talent for the trapeze took him all over the world…. He met his future wife Laurence, in the Dominican Republic and taught her the trapeze…

Brent van Rensburg
Zip Zap: Co-founder and CEO
Brent: Came back for a 6 week holiday to show my girl friend CT. I hadn’t been home for 15 years SA was in times of change we thought we should stay and make a difference by using circus as the tool try to bridge gaps between children

Laurence Esteve
Zip Zap: Co-founder and CEO
Laurence: Because we came from the circus and in circus you value diversity and we arrive in SA and people were packing and like we know how to deal with kids and its just kids from different backgrounds and circus will be the glue.
V/O 3 sec and 4 sec
Phelelane Ndakrokra joined Zip Zap 9 years ago. He was living in a shelter, his mother was on the streets.

Phelelani Ndakrokra: I am trying to find what is my limit I will never give up because of the background where I came from it doesn’t matter how difficult it is but everything is possible.
Claire If not Zip Zap where?
Phelelani: Probably still on the street and maybe prison I am not sure because me I was born on the street I grew up on the street and I stayed there for 15 years so I probably will still be there.

Link : Last year alone 2042 children were put though Zip Zap’s 8 programmes and each one of these children attended free of charge

V/O
Zip Zap is runs as a non profit organisation.

Brent: You use circus skills to uplift children who have difficulties whether it is drugs or Violence…not expected to become a professional performer in a circus school…
The kids that come here they find a home here and a sense of belonging and a safe place to play we just want to be the lighthouse.

Siyabonga Swelindawo: We live as a family we laugh together we cry together and we fight as well, so it is a family. I started as a young boy 11 years old and I am still involved still love the family.

V/O
Siyabonga Swelindawo, is a passionate juggler, he runs Zip Zap’s out reach programmes.

Siyabonga : Juggling has been one of the things that has changed my life at Zip Zap from juggling I learnt a lot of things I learnt confidence I learnt discipline even if I drop a juggling ball I have to pick it up and carry on.

V/O 10 sec
As Zip Zap’s family grew….Brent and Laurence became parents to Sabine and Saskia…who almost immediately became part of their circus troupe.

Victoria ENGELHORN
Chair: Zip Zap Trust
Victoria: Not just a circus act so much more important: it’s learning how to trust it’s learning how to be honest, its learning how to be respectful and if you look in a circus act if you don’t trust the person that is going to catch you you might just fall.

V/O 9 sec
Victoria Engelhorn heads up the Zip Zap Trust. The circus performances pay for running costs but the trust has to constantly fund raise.
Victoria: You see Kids that are acting, as if they had been doing this for their whole life and they think aah these people don’t need help but we do because behind all of this is the out reach programme are huge and we work with kids we have HIV we work with Kid that are from SOS primary schools and its all about bringing them in showing them the opportunities that Zip Zap provides. ….on each level Trompie so amazing but he also needs to learn more so it’s a constant growth.

Trompie: If ZZ wasn’t here I believe I will still be robbing people staying on the street not looking for a better thing to do.

Link: For years Brent’s goal was to get a permanent home for ZZ that included a home for the performers and this new facility of theirs is the only circus school of its kind on the continent.

V/O 9 sec
This week Zip Zap will leave for their 35th International Tour, in these 26 years they have played in over 20 counties.

Trompie: It was super lovely my first time it was super lovely because it was super cold everyone was smiling I was the only one !!! I couldn’t smile I was my nose you could see it change colour.

Claire: And like to see other come through ZZ role model?
Phelelani: It reminds me of when I was still younger and I was started to join ZZ I also looked up to a lot of guys now I need to watch what I am doing.

Brent: You know this is not a job to us this is a life calling when you know you have been a small part of changing a child’s life and making a difference that is enough reason to wake up every day and feel blessed

V/O 9 and a half sec sec
As they say in the industry, circus is the place where dreams can come true…. And even when the going is hard, the act must go on.

Phelelani: Sometimes it happens when you have a problem you have to go on stage that’s a nice way to express yourself and bring your anger in your act but in a good way.
I have done it, Shouting on stage release my anger felt so much better and then would go back stage and cry.
Claire: Powerful lesson because some of these kids like you tough backgrounds bright shining light my friend.
Thank you
